sections.sectionSummaryBrief: To properly rectify a stumble, repentance alone is insufficient; one must add the "words" of Torah and mitzvos, which require precise measurement.

translations.translation: And he continues with the verse, "Take with you words," etc.
For in order to properly rectify the stumbling
(that which he stumbled with his foot),
the matter of repentance—the nullification of selfhood that is brought about through it—is not sufficient; this is effected through confession of words,
the matter of the letters, as explained in Sefer HaMitzvos of the Tzemach Tzedek.
For the ultimate purpose of repentance is the service of Torah and mitzvos
(and as above regarding the matter of repentance and good deeds),
and to this he adds, "Take with you words" of Torah and mitzvos, as explained in Likkutei Torah on the verse.
And these words are specifically in measurement.
For it is not necessary to mention regarding the Oral Torah, since the study of the Oral Torah must specifically be with understanding and comprehension,
it is therefore necessarily in measurement,
but even the Written Torah, although in the Written Torah the matter of comprehension is not so relevant,
nevertheless, even in the Written Torah there must be measurement,
and on the contrary,
the measurement of the Written Torah is greater than the measurement of the Oral Torah,
for in the Written Torah, the letters, the crowns, and the cantillation notes must be with utmost precision.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The ultimate purpose of repentance is not only forgiveness but the transformation of sins into merits, achieved through the aspect of "Kol" (All) which elevates sin.

translations.translation: And he continues with the verse, "Say to Him, 'All will You bear iniquity.'"
And the explanation is,
that the ultimate matter of repentance is not only that sins be forgiven, but that the very intentional sins be transformed into merits,
and this is why even after "Return, O Israel," it must be said, "Say to Him, 'All will You bear iniquity,'"
"Tisa avon" is the matter of "Nosei avon" (He bears iniquity),
not only that He will suppress our iniquities and cast all their sins into the depths of the sea,
but that He also "bears iniquity,"
that He carries and elevates the iniquity,
that the sins become merits, as explained at length in Ohr HaTorah.
And this matter
("Tisa avon")
is accomplished through "Say to Him, 'All,'"
"All" is that which He is—He is All and includes everything,
and therefore "Tisa avon,"
that He bears even the iniquity and transforms it into merits.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Through complete repentance, one achieves the elevation of "our lips as bulls," reaching a level above physical offerings, ultimately to the aspect of the "Face of Hashem."

translations.translation: And he continues with the verse, "And we will render [the words of] our lips as bulls,"
meaning that through the completeness of the repentance of "Return, O Israel," etc., they effect completeness in the matter of the offerings after "you have stumbled in your iniquity,"
for the interpretation of "And we will render [the words of] our lips as bulls" is not only that our lips are a substitute for bulls, but rather that our lips effect completeness in the "bulls,"
for "our lips" is the matter of prayer,
the matter of offerings in a spiritual sense,
which is higher than the matter of physical offerings,

and analogous to this, even in the time of the Temple when there was the offering of sacrifices in their simple sense, even then there needed to be the matter of Israel standing, Levites at their platform, and priests in their service, and particularly the service of the priests—it was "in secrecy and with a willing heart."
And this is what is written, "And we will render [the words of] our lips as bulls" after "Return, O Israel," etc.,
for this matter
("And we will render [the words of] our lips as bulls")
is the elevation that is brought about through repentance,
that which reaches elevation after elevation,
above even the matter of offerings,
until it reaches the level of the "Face of Hashem."
And as it is written,
"Seek My face—Your face, Hashem, I will seek,"
that through "Seek My face," which is the matter of repentance,
through this, "Your face, Hashem, I will seek."
For in the manner of drawing down from above to below, it is written,
"And you will see My back, but My face shall not be seen,"
but in the manner of elevation,
they reach the level of "Your face, Hashem."
